site.name: Superiso Studio
site.description: Superiso Studio is an architecture and interior design practice in Singapore, shaping homes around the lives and stories they hold.

quote.text: Every great design begins with an even better story
quote.author: Lorinda Mamo

principles.title: Design together
principles.body: We collaborate with the people we design for, and with the makers who build it. A better result comes from more voices, not fewer.

principles.title: Make room for play
principles.body: A home should hold emotion as well as function. We look for the moments of delight, surprise and warmth that make a space feel lived in.

principles.title: Tread lightly
principles.body: Sustainable design should be ordinary, not exceptional. We work with what is already there and choose materials that will last.

process.title: Concept
process.body: It begins with listening. Your routines, your aspirations and the character of the place become the starting point for everything that follows.

process.title: Designing
process.body: Ideas take shape through light, proportion and material. We explore the possibilities together, from the larger plan down to the smallest joint.

process.title: Executing
process.body: Thought becomes space. The design is carried through on site with care, keeping the original story at the heart of the finished place.

projects.title: Resort Living
projects.summary: A simple East Coast house for a couple, reimagined as an everyday retreat.
body: The brief was deceptively simple: turn an ordinary landed house into somewhere that feels like arriving on holiday. Not a themed resort, but the particular calm of a place where the outside is always close by.

An arched pavilion opens the living spaces directly onto the pool and garden, so the boundary between inside and out is barely drawn. Timber, stone and planting carry through the house, and a frangipani tree anchors the terrace it was built around.

projects.title: Childhood Memories
projects.summary: A family of four moving back into the home one of them grew up in.
body: Returning to a childhood home is a particular kind of brief. The house already holds a story; the work is to make room for the next one without erasing what came before.

The original roof structure was opened up and left exposed, giving the upper floor height and light it never had. Below, a calm palette of timber, stone and off-white lets the family's own life supply the colour.

projects.title: K+M Apartment
projects.summary: A first home for a couple of dentists, made for unwinding at the end of long days.
body: Two demanding careers, and a home that needed to do the opposite of a clinic. The apartment is warm where their working days are clinical, and quiet where they are busy.
Fluted timber screens filter the entrance and living areas, giving the plan a sense of depth without closing it down. Storage is absorbed into the walls, so the rooms stay clear and the eye can rest.

projects.title: Terrace Apartment
projects.summary: An apartment for a family who cook, and who like a full table.
body: The roof terrace was the reason for the whole project. It had the space for a proper outdoor kitchen, and a family who would actually use it several times a week.
Indoors, the plan was rebalanced around gathering: a generous dining table at the centre, and storage that keeps the everyday clutter of a busy household out of sight.

projects.title: Chef's Fillet
projects.summary: One bold gesture, threading the common spaces of a four-room flat together.
body: A four-room flat gives you a fixed envelope and a limited budget. The opportunity is in deciding where to spend both.
Here it goes into a single continuous move that links entrance, kitchen, dining and living into one legible space. Everything else stays quiet and pale, so the gesture does the work.

projects.title: House on House
projects.summary: A new home built on top of an existing two-storey terrace, making room for a family to grow.
body: Rather than start again, the project adds. A new storey is built over the existing two-storey terrace, giving the owners the space they need without giving up the house they already have.
The addition is read as its own volume, set back and lighter than the masonry below, with a planted terrace in between. The result is a house that shows its two chapters rather than hiding the join.

projects.title: Courtyard House
projects.summary: A corner terrace reworked around a courtyard for a family of four.
body: Corner plots give you something most terraces never have: a second face to the street, and the light that comes with it.

The proposal turns the house inward around a courtyard, so that rooms borrow light and air from the middle of the plan rather than competing for the perimeter. A pitched roof carries the form back to its neighbours.

projects.title: Secret Garden
projects.summary: A mixed-use proposal that gives its ground floor back to the street as public garden.
body: The studio's largest proposal to date, and the one that tests its ideas at civic scale. Apartments sit above a commercial ground floor on a busy Novena corner.
The move is to hollow out the base. A planted garden is carved through the ground plane and left open to the street, so the building gives something back to the neighbourhood it sits in.
